transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, thank you. I guess what brings me in is... I just can't seem to get past how rough and worn my face and hands look. It's all the deep cracks, the spots, the sagging skin. 

Whenever I have to go into town, I feel like every banker or county person is just staring right at it. My wife says I just look like a man who's worked outdoors his whole life, but I can't stop focusing on how bad it is. It really bothers me.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your face and hands in mirrors or other reflective surfaces throughout the day?

Yeah, I do. It happens a lot before I leave for a loan meeting, or if we've got a craft-fair table to set up. I'll just keep checking the bathroom mirror... and then I get out to the truck and start checking the truck mirror, too. I'll be turning my hat this way and that, trying to see how it looks. And my hands, I'm always looking at them and comparing them to the younger workers' hands. Honestly, I do it until I've just wasted time I really should be using to get work done on the farm.

Outside of concerns about your appearance, do you find yourself having other repetitive thoughts or routines, like repeatedly checking locks, excessive cleaning, or needing things arranged in a specific way?

No, not really. I mean, I make sure the barn is locked up at night and the equipment is put away, but that's just normal farm stuff. I don't go back and check it over and over again or anything. And I'm definitely not an excessive cleaner. It's really just the stuff with my skin that I get stuck on.
If you felt completely satisfied with how your skin and hands looked, would you still feel anxious or uncomfortable interacting with people in town?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I used to be just fine talking to folks at the bank or the feed store. If I didn't have to worry about them staring at all these cracks and spots, I'd be perfectly comfortable going into town. It's really just knowing how bad I look that makes me want to avoid people. If my skin and hands were fine, I'd be fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits excessive preoccupation with perceived flaws or defects in physical appearance (deep cracks, spots, and sagging skin on face and hands) that appear slight or normal to others. This preoccupation is accompanied by repetitive behaviors (frequent mirror-checking, comparing hands to others) and causes significant distress, social avoidance, and time wasted from work, meeting criteria for Body Dysmorphic Disorder (ICD-10: F45.22). General obsessive-compulsive disorder and primary social anxiety disorder were ruled out.
